stumbles.quote: violations were 42 of 43 in every form
stumbles.why: Unclear what the 43 items are (prompts? trials?) and what 'every form' covers. It's also unclear whether 42 of 43 violating means near-total non-compliance.

stumbles.quote: Naming a forbidden word raised its probability by ~2.5 log-odds.
stumbles.why: It doesn't say compared to what baseline, or whether this was in the same model and experiment. The link to the capitalisation result is unclear.

stumbles.quote: Its 22,100-doc corpus held one capitalised instruction.
stumbles.why: 'Its' is ambiguous. It probably means the model's training corpus, but that isn't stated. It also isn't clear why this matters or how it connects to the earlier findings.

point: Capitalising an instruction didn't make a tiny model (Baguettotron, 321M) obey it, and naming a forbidden word made it more likely to say it, possibly because its training corpus almost never contained capitalised instructions.
